title: The interface is discharged
statement:
Fix the global finite-field and coefficient data of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]: $k$ is an algebraic closure of the finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes. Use the concrete operations and projection transformation of that operation datum, with derived-complete integral coefficients, rationalization at $E$, and common finite coefficient stages at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

For every $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ (bounded constructible, with finite Tor amplitude required of $L$), the canonical map
$$
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\longrightarrow Rf_!(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L)
$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $K,L$, compatible with composition (the associativity pentagon), compactification comparisons, finite reduction on the stated finite-Tor domains, scalar extension, and $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ when $f$ is proper. The formula is on the small pro-etale sites of the operation datum; at integral coefficients tensor and pullback are completed, and the field stages use their rational and common-stage extensions. At the rational and algebraically closed stages, when $X=X_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ and $Y=Y_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ for separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes $X_0,Y_0$ and $f$ is the geometric base change of a separated finite-type $k_0$-morphism $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$, the formula restricts to the Weil categories [def-wf-weil-category] of $X_0$ and $Y_0$, with tensor Frobenius as in [def-wf-tensor-product].

Thus every obligation of the concrete interface [fix-prop-projection-formula] is discharged, unconditionally on its stated domains. The discharge uses no duality theorem: it concerns $Rf_!$, pullback and tensor, logically before Verdier duality. The ordinary-direct-image formula is asserted here only for proper $f$.

proof.text: Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum], not a six-functor datum with unverified axioms. Its coefficient stages are exactly $A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and its item (3) fixes the actual projection transformation. Its item (2) fixes compact support, the composition comparisons and proper coincidence. The final paragraph explicitly says this datum names operations and construction data and does not assert smooth purity or Verdier biduality. These are precisely the concrete data and coefficient conventions in the statement, so the concrete theorem used next applies without assuming projection invertibility as an axiom.

Apply the existing concrete theorem [fix-prop-projection-formula] to $f,K,L$. Its quantified domain is separated finite-type $f$, $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, exactly ours, and its displayed morphism is the specified projection transformation, with the same direction and endpoints. It asserts that this map is an isomorphism at every coefficient stage. Thus the finite coefficient, completed integral, rational and algebraically closed cases are all obtained on their actual coefficient categories. In particular no finite Tor condition is added to finite-level $K$. This is a use of an already existing theorem, not a new node restating one of these cases.

source.place: fix-prop-projection-formula.md, statement through the displayed isomorphism

proof.text: The compatibility sentence of [fix-prop-projection-formula] asserts naturality in both inputs, compatibility with the composition law and its associativity pentagon, the compactification comparisons, finite reduction on the stated finite-Tor domains, scalar extension, and proper coincidence. These are the interface obligations with the same maps, not newly chosen isomorphisms. Retain exactly its finite-reduction qualification: this does not impose finite Tor amplitude on an arbitrary finite-level $K$ just to obtain the isomorphism, or assert reduction of a field-coefficient object without an integral representative. For proper $f$, the theorem identifies this same map with the ordinary-direct-image projection formula via $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$; it asserts no such formula for nonproper $f$.

source.place: fix-prop-projection-formula.md, compatibility sentence and final proper-case sentence

proof.text: For the Weil clause assume exactly the additional finite-field model in the statement. The Weil sentence of [fix-prop-projection-formula] requires $X=X_0\otimes_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ for separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes and $f$ the base change of $f_0$. Those are now the hypotheses in force. That sentence gives an isomorphism in the specified Weil categories at the rational and algebraically closed stages, with their specified tensor. No descent model is assumed for the earlier non-Weil assertion, and no integral lift of a Weil automorphism is required.

source.place: fix-prop-projection-formula.md, Weil-category clause (with the finite-field model made explicit in the reviewed DAG statement)

proof.text: The preceding steps supply the isomorphism, all its coefficient stages and the compatibility and Weil clauses, so every obligation of the interface holds. The only theorem invoked in these steps is the concrete projection-formula theorem; no duality assertion is invoked. The no-duality sentence is a provenance assertion about this discharge, not an inference from an axiom of an abstract six-functor datum: the source proof explicitly finishes by saying that its constructions and comparisons of the same projection map use neither smooth purity nor Verdier duality. The existing concrete split likewise proves the formula by finite projection, reduction of the actual integral map, and coefficient and site transport, before any duality theorem.

source.place: sk-rem-sf-pf-done.proof.md, last sentence; fix-prop-projection-formula.proof.md, last sentence

theorem compactSupportProjectionFormula
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} {C : D.CoefficientDatum}
    {E : Type u} [Field E] [Algebra (Padic C.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic C.l) E] {n : ℕ} {hn : 1 ≤ n}
    (S : SixFunctorOperationDatum D C E n hn) :
    CompactSupportFiniteProjection.Laws S.toSixFunctorFiniteOperations ∧
    CompactSupportProjectionLaws S.higher.integral S.higher.integralTensor
      S.higher.integralExchange S.integralFiniteTorDomain ∧
    CompactSupportProjectionLaws S.higher.rational S.higher.rationalTensor
      S.higher.rationalExchange (fun _ _ ↦ True) ∧
    CompactSupportProjectionLaws S.closure.commonStage S.closure.commonStageTensor
      S.closure.commonStageExchange (fun _ _ ↦ True) ∧
    (∀ m : ℕ, CompactSupportFiniteProjection.Laws
      (S.integralNormalization.finiteLevels m)) ∧
    ∀ E₀ : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields C.l C.Qbar,
      CompactSupportProjectionLaws (S.closure.coefficientStages E₀).integral
        (S.closure.coefficientStages E₀).integralTensor
        (S.closure.coefficientStages E₀).integralExchange
        (fun X K ↦ finiteTorConstructibleIntegral C.l
          (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} C.l C.Qbar E₀) X.obj.left K.obj) ∧
      CompactSupportProjectionLaws (S.closure.coefficientStages E₀).rational
        (S.closure.coefficientStages E₀).rationalTensor
        (S.closure.coefficientStages E₀).rationalExchange (fun _ _ ↦ True) ∧
      ∀ m : ℕ, CompactSupportFiniteProjection.Laws
        ((S.coefficientIntegralNormalization E₀).finiteLevels m)
